why: Celebrating a finished work, crediting its makers, and thanking allies after the close run through the same retrospective posts, so deciding whether pride or credit is the point recurs across several rooms' year-end threads.

why.T3-001: Members of the room themselves post invented or ambiguous hardware fakes as true for April 1 (a Vega lineup prank image, a fake leaked slideshow, a fake Ryzen unlock rickroll, a retirement announcement) and one later reveals the firmware fix was an April Fools joke, so the room stages its own fakes rather than testing an outside claim.

why.T3-095: The practice is settling whether a claim the room did not stage is a joke: the WCCF 'Vega Leak', a WCCF-hosted slide deck and Eurocom's announcement are checked by date, source and end-notes, which is T3-095's gate rather than the room's own fakes.

why.T3-009: Members mark the room's own work as achieved: the flag survived the final canvas, the shared post hit number one, and they made the front page — celebration of the finished work.
why.T3-043: Other concepts have members claiming or negotiating credit for named parts: a user spreads the idea that ended the subs' war and is not credited, and another claims a part in shaping the crescent, which is crediting-claiming rather than celebration.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-009's gate (marking the room's own work as achieved) does not reach the concepts where members claim a specific personal part or negotiate who gets credit for an idea (C1250899, C1311431, C1080007), so a single T3-009 placement would drop the credit side entirely.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1311431 claims a part in shaping the crescent and C1250899 negotiates credit for spreading the shared idea — members crediting or claiming their own part in the work, which is T3-043's gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-043, since the celebrating concepts hold more; dropping it loses the credit negotiation over the crescent and the shared idea.

why.T3-022: The Radeon mark is gone (cannot be found, converted into redcorner) and the room restarts an AMD mark elsewhere, taking red dots at 270,630 and opening a logo in the red corner — moving and restarting after losing the spot, T3-022 rather than a first-choice spot.

why.T3-151: A visitor offers to build and maintain CompSoc's image and in the same breath asks the neighbours to maintain theirs, with the vandalism explained as why that mutual upkeep is useful — help offered in return for help, T3-151 rather than unasked help.

why.T3-005: An attack on the AMD mark is under way (raided by SNEK, NVIDIA out to destroy, under attack) and members answer with alarms, rallying cries and hold-the-line calls — defence against attackers, not mere watching and cleaning (T3-021).

why.T3-022: The void wiped the CompSoc work out and the same passage votes to reestablish elsewhere in the top left — a move and restart after the work was erased, T3-022.

why.T3-016: One member asks what the canvas is for and whether it enters a hall of fame, and another explains it as a fun April Fools joke pointing to the sub — questions and answers about the event itself, T3-016.

why.T3-072: The retrospective thanks other rooms by name and tells who stood with the room: gratitude to the Mareşals, diplomats, engineers and neighbourhood allies in the Sheev's Neighborhood coalition, plus thanks to all who defended the clay.
why.T3-117: Other concepts register the end of the event itself: it finally ended, what to do with life now, hoping place returns, and signing off with a goodbye after defending in Discord — marking the canvas's end, which T3-072's ally-thanking does not reach.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-072's gate (thanking other rooms and telling who stood with the room) does not reach the concepts that register the canvas's own ending and the goodbye (C0985765, C1210951, C0273042, C0976699), so a single T3-072 placement would fail to carry the end-marking.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0985765 says it finally ended, C0273042 hopes place returns, C0976699 signs off with a goodbye — members marking the canvas's end, T3-117's gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-117, since the thanking and ally-naming hold more concepts; dropping it loses the end-of-event regrets and the sign-off.

why.T3-026: Members announce that CompSoc's mark is on the canvas with its place and pictures — an initial coordinate, a corrected coordinate and linked images showing where it stands, T3-026 rather than a discovery of an unknown mark (T3-082).

why.T3-004: Members work out what the mark should look like: whether the arrow is green or red, whether to keep the shape and letters, what colour the official logo guide allows, how wide the letters are — the design's colours, borders and lettering settled and corrected.
why.T3-066: Other concepts put that design choice to the room as a vote: a strawpoll on the logo colour, a poll whose overwhelming consensus was green, and calls that the colour be settled by a strawpoll — a choice about the work put to a vote.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-004's gate (working out the mark's look and correcting it) does not reach the concepts where the colour decision is handed to a strawpoll and a vote is demanded to settle it (C1332430, C0926826, C0398700), so a single T3-004 placement would drop the voting mechanism.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1332430 and C0926826 put the logo colour to a strawpoll and C0398700 calls for a vote to settle the debacle — a choice about the work put to the room, T3-066's gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-066, since the colour-and-shape argument holds most concepts; dropping it loses the strawpoll that settled the colour.

why.T3-016: Most concepts orient newcomers by explaining the event itself: the five-minute pixel rule, how to pick a colour and click a pixel, why subs are making pictures, what the everywhere-today activity is — explanation of what the canvas is.
why.T3-070: Other concepts post a location for placers to follow: a direct r/place coordinate link, a request that the coordinate link be standard, and a link directing a confused reader to the logo — coordinates shared for people to act on.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-016's gate (explaining the event to newcomers) does not reach the concepts that hand placers a location to act on (C0588551, C0420404, C0927715), so a single T3-016 placement would lose the coordinates themselves.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0588551 shares the r/place coordinate link, C0420404 asks for the direct coordinate link to be standard, and C0927715 directs a reader to the logo — coordinates posted for placers to follow, T3-070's gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-070, since the explanations hold most concepts; dropping it loses the shared coordinate links.

why.T3-011: After doing their AMD part a member spreads effort to help r/thenetherlands, and another offers to help r/Nvidia make its logo — pixels sent to another room's work with nothing asked in return, T3-011 rather than a trade (T3-151).

why.T3-001: The poster twice apologises for leaving the discussion text out of the leak thread they posted, which is housekeeping on the room's own staged April Fools fake rather than an outside claim being framed; the leak post is the material's only anchor.

why.T3-022: Same practice as position 4: the Radeon mark is gone (cannot be found, converted into redcorner) and the room restarts an AMD mark elsewhere, taking red dots at 270,630 and opening a logo in the red corner — moving and restarting after losing the spot, T3-022.
